source.title: Controlling Grokking with Nonlinearity and Data Symmetry

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking in modular addition and how activation functions and network width affect its timing, using a two-layer MLP rather than the original study's Transformer setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training/test-accuracy behavior for modular-addition models and entropy behavior during training. PCA patterns, weight correlations, and factorization results are not rows because they do not themselves measure the claim versions' named behaviors. Weight decay is used, but the paper does not test the efficiency account or optimizer/numerical-artifact challenge.
record.test_reason: The paper trains a two-layer MLP without embeddings on one-hot modular addition, rather than the original Transformer, and reports train/test accuracy curves in which test accuracy rises long after training accuracy. That bears on V1. Its other measures do not test the versions as named. Weight entropy is not a circuit-formation measure (V2). Activation and width changes are not initialization scale or weight norm, and all data are algorithmic (V3). Nothing tests V4–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors conclude that grokking onset can be delayed by adding a linear (odd) component to an even activation, and that greater width or depth increases the train–test delay. They also conclude that grokking occurs even with aperiodic weights and without visible PCA structure, and that PCA projections of last-layer weights can factor a non-prime modulus. Results hold with partially removed data symmetries if the training fraction is raised. Weight entropy and weight correlations are proposed as metrics of learning and grokking.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a two-layer MLP without embeddings on one-hot modular addition, with Adam and weight decay; the original source is described as observing grokking in Transformers. The paper also considers activation, width, and depth changes.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking timing varies with activation-function form and coefficient, hidden-layer width, network depth, training fraction, and data symmetry. Exact timing values are generally not reported in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Grokking onset timing depends on network nonlinearity. Adding an odd linear term to an x² activation delays test-accuracy rise, with epochs before grokking decreasing as a grows. Reducing width from 256 to 64 shrinks the train–test delay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The grokking delay can be tuned by activation-function parity and network width or depth in algorithmic tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-weight entropy falls during training fit, rises while test accuracy groks, and falls again after test accuracy peaks (x²). With x+x² the fall comes after test accuracy peaks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight entropy tracks, and per the authors predicts, the generalization phase of grokking.

record.problems: Most accuracy and timing comparisons are presented as figures without numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The paper does not provide a systematic training-set-size versus delay sweep, and several changed-data conditions reach less than perfect test accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: PCA projections, weight-correlation patterns, factorization, and weight magnitudes are omitted because they do not measure a behavior named by the tested claim versions. No other claim-bearing results were omitted.

untested.parts: There is no controlled sweep of grokking delay against training-set size. Only scattered changes to P and TRAIN_FRAC are reported, without delay values.
No generalizing circuit is identified over training, there is no progress measure of circuit formation, and there is no tracking of memorization removal.
Untested in full: only modular addition is used, and initialization scale and weight norm are not varied.
Untested in full: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Untested in full: weight decay is always on and is not varied; no critical dataset size or ungrokking test.
Untested: no comparison of learned algorithms across runs or architectures, beyond qualitative weight observations.
Untested in full: Adam is used throughout, and no optimizer or numerical controls are applied.

missing.what: x² sign(x) activation: grokking 'does not occur' (no row).
Commutation-restricted data with x+2x² activation, or a 3-layer model, gives results 'similar' to the 0.85 max test accuracy.
Decreasing P to 20 'reduces ... the effect of grokking'. At TRAIN_FRAC 0.7, test accuracy declines after reaching 1, so 0.8 was used. This bears on dataset-size dependence but is qualitative.

Some last-layer weights are quasi-sinusoidal with sharp Fourier peaks, while others are nonperiodic yet grokking persists, which the authors say contradicts Gromov. Under weight decay, a fraction of last-layer weights decays below 1e-41 many epochs after grokking without affecting test accuracy. These are qualitative observations relevant to the Fourier-circuit and cleanup picture, with no time course relative to the jump.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. All accuracy and timing results are figure-only, with no numeric onset epochs or uncertainty. The reader's V3 links were dropped: changing activation or width on modular addition does not match V3's non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale/weight-norm switch. The V2 links were dropped because weight entropy is not a circuit-formation progress measure.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not systematically establish that optimization delay grows as the training set shrinks; reported changes in data fraction and dataset size are not a controlled delay-versus-training-set-size sweep.

The paper measures weight entropy over training and relates it to grokking, but does not identify a generalizing circuit, track removal of memorizing components, or test a Fourier algorithm forming gradually.
Only modular-addition data are tested. The paper changes activation functions and width/depth, not initialization scale or weight norm, and does not test image, text, or molecule data.
LLM pretraining and fine-tuning on realistic data are not tested.
No efficiency comparison, critical dataset-size prediction, or ungrokking test is reported.
The paper does not compare identifiable algorithms learned across runs.
The paper does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax explanations.

relationships.condition: Odd activation (x³) and modular-addition data with symmetries removed
relationships.reason: With x³ there is no grokking and test accuracy peaks then falls (r7). With the commutation symmetry removed, post-grok test accuracy peaks at 0.85, or stays below unity at P=75 (r13, r14). With further restriction, grokking is absent at TRAIN_FRAC 0.5 and reaches 0.984 only at 0.8 (r15).
relationships.display_finding: Cubic activation prevented grokking; removing commutation symmetry yielded a peak of 85% or accuracy below 100% at P=75, while further restriction prevented grokking at a 0.5 training fraction but allowed 98.4% at 0.8.
